history.gap: The section is a well-set table of contents, not a designed moment: ten identical rows of right-aligned serif + hairline + muted caption, with the entire right third of the container (from ~975px to the 1100px rule) left dead and the CTA shrunk to a 12px smallcap at the bottom. At the bar, the ten terms would earn one typographic event — a single term set at display scale, a hover state that swaps in a definition or a chart glyph, or the captions pulled out to the right margin so the row spans the full measure — and the "Kom erbij" CTA would carry the weight of the section's only action instead of hiding under a dashed ticket-rule cliché. On mobile the centred CTA also breaks the strict left axis every row has established.
history.motion: Restrained section-level fades and a soft rise as the block enters; no per-row stagger, so the ten-item list arrives as one slab rather than a cadence.
history.verdict: A wins on craft: its hairlines, numerals, scale contrast and colour restraint are disciplined, though it is a handsome index rather than a section anyone will remember. B has the more distinctive world and the better photography, but a Site of the Day cannot ship with unreadable body copy, a strike-through nav and word-spacing bugs from its own animation.

At the bar the detail panel earns its width — a two-column definition, a rule-set of terms, a real (not zigzag placeholder) schematic that changes per item — and the heading is designed (tighter tracking, optical size, a numeral or eyebrow tied to the list) rather than simply set large.
history.motion: Fade-up reveals of list and chart with a scroll-progress line and active-section nav state — restrained and clean, but stock choreography with no distinctive easing.
history.verdict: A is a coherent, well-aligned dark editorial system — mono numerals, gold hairlines, consistent insets, a mobile list that actually reads — let down by a dead right column and a placeholder chart, so it is "fine", not shortlist. B has the more distinctive, atmospheric world, but a jury cannot forgive illegible copy, a label colliding with the logo, and mobile nav rendering bugs; A wins on craft while neither reaches Site of the Day.
